sample_unit: neonates (15,343 hours of continuous EEG; 2,455 seizures)

links.outcome: False detections per day and seizure-level detection tradeoffs across three neonatal seizure detectors
links.effect: NSD1 generated 46 FD/day (IQR 22-82) versus 3.2 for NSD2 and 2.8 for Persyst-15 (P<0.0001). Seizure detection was 63% for NSD1, 35% for NSD2, and 60% for Persyst-15.
links.quote: NSD1 generated significantly more FDs (46 FD/day, IQR 22-82) than NSD2 (3.2 IQR 1.2-9.3) and Persyst-15 (2.8 IQR 1.1-6.2; P < 0.0001).

screen.reason: Evaluates clinical performance trade-offs (sensitivity vs. false detection alarm burden and latency) of three AI seizure detection algorithms on a retrospective clinical EEG dataset without testing a specific deployment safeguard or intervention.
